Judas Iscariot. One of the twelve apostles of Jesus who became notorious for betraying Jesus to the religious authorities in exchange for thirty pieces of silver, the price of a slave in ancient law. He identified Jesus to soldiers and priests with a kiss in the Garden of Gethsemane, enabling his arrest. Before his betrayal, he had been the treasurer of the apostolic group, trusted to manage funds. After Jesus's condemnation, Judas expressed remorse and attempted to return the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests. According to Matthew's account, he died by suicide, hanging himself. In John's Gospel, he is described as possessed by Satan, emphasizing the spiritual evil behind his betrayal. His act of betrayal was prophesied in Psalm 41:9, which Jesus himself quoted, linking his betrayal to scripture. Judas became the archetypal symbol of betrayal in Western culture, his name synonymous with treachery.
